name: M8a_test
title: Bayesian version of the M8a test for positive selection

args.name: submodel
args.description: The model, as a function of dN/dS

args.name: n
args.description: Number of categories approximating the Beta distribution

args.name: mu
args.description: The mean of the Beta distribution

args.name: v
args.description: The normalized Beta variance Var(omega)/(mu*(1-mu)); 0 < v < 1

args.name: posP
args.description: Fraction of sites in the additional neutral or positively selected category

args.name: posW
args.description: dN/dS of the additional category when posSelection=1

args.name: posSelection
args.description: Model indicator: 0 for M8a, 1 for M8

description:
A Bayesian version of the M8a likelihood-ratio test for positive selection, comparing:

   H0: M8a (posSelection=0), no positive selection
   H1: M8 (posSelection=1), some positive selection

The additional category has dN/dS=1 under H0, where posW is ignored, and dN/dS=posW under H1. The Beta component is present under both hypotheses. The default prior restricts posW to values greater than 1.

The default prior gives each hypothesis probability 0.5. With these equal prior odds, the Bayes factor for H1 against H0 equals the posterior odds Pr(H1 | data)/Pr(H0 | data).

PrPosSelection records the conditional probability of H1 given the data and other parameters. Its posterior mean estimates Pr(H1 | data), often more accurately than the mean of posSelection. The statreport tool uses LogOddsPosSelection to report the corresponding posterior log odds accurately, even when the probability is extremely close to 0 or 1. Do not average LogOddsPosSelection directly.

Including an explicit neutral category in the null model reduces the risk of mistaking a mixture of conserved and neutral sites for positive selection.

The Beta component uses Gauss-Jacobi quadrature with generally unequal category weights. There are n+1 categories in total.

The Beta-component mean mu and normalized variance v have independent Uniform(0,1) default priors.

citation.title: Pervasive Adaptive Evolution in Mammalian Fertilization Proteins
